text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and Oman's Sultan Qaboos bin Said discussed Egypt's moves to save peace and ways to boost bilateral relations. The leaders's talks in the Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh covered a number of Arab and regional issues, including challenges facing peace, cementing regional security and stability in the Gulf region.
- A conference of the Arab information ministers will condemn in its resolutions today the U.S. Congress decision to move the U.S. embassy to Jerusalem from Tel Aviv.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa left Cairo yesterday morning for Hong Kong to take part in the island's handover celebrations.
- Mubarak receives a message from Emir of Bahrain Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa.

- The Kuwaiti Fund for Arab Economic Development extended a 15 million Kuwaiti dinar ($50 million) loan to finance the second stage of the Egyptian Social Fund. The loan carries a two percent interest rate and will be repaid within 30 years after a 10-year grace period.
- Three terrorists were hanged yesterday. The terrorists had killed three people and injured four others in eight terrorist attacks.
